To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

strong coupling between light and molecules (polaritonic chemistry) can be used to manipulate the photochemical properties of molecules, and that this manipulation is not limited to simple systems, but can also be used in complex systems such as azobenzene.
the photoisomerization of azobenzene can be manipulated by the strong coupling with light and that this manipulation can be achieved by tuning the polaritonic conic intersection.

(i) strong coupling between molecules and light can be used to manipulate photochemistry; (ii) polaritonic photochemistry is characterized by coherent oscillations between polariton states; (iii) polaritonic chemistry can be quenched through the trapping of the polaritons in dead-end states; (iv) polaritons can alter the photochemical reaction path and the quantum yield of a photochemical reaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of computational photochemistry methods to investigate photochemical processes in the strong light–molecular coupling regime and the analysis of their impact on the photochemical reactivity of realistic systems.
the development of new computational approaches to the simulation of light-induced processes in complex systems.
the photochemistry of azobenzene, a prototypical molecule with two isomer states, cis-azobenzene and trans-azobenzened.

the strong coupling of light and matter offers a new strategy for manipulating the photochemistry of organic molecules, and we have provided a first glimpse of the potential of this approach.
